newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's oil buffer fund deficit 2.21 billion peso.
newsitem.headline: Manila's oil buffer fund deficit 2.21 billion peso.

text.p: The Philippine energy department said on Thursday that the deficit of the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund (OPSF) stood at 2.21 billion pesos as of end-July, wider than the 1.96 billion pesos in June.
Energy Minister Francisco Viray said the increased deficit was brought about by outstanding claims of the oil companies at 203.4 million pesos in July.

The OPSF is a fund aimed at ensuring stable domestic prices despite fluctuations in international oil prices and foreign exchange rates. The buffer fund will be phased out by March 1997 if the government pushes through with the full deregulation of the oil industry.

Energy Minister Francisco Viray said the oil fund deficit was expected to reach 2.3 billion pesos as of August 13, the day prior to the government's implementation of an automatic oil price formula as part of the partial oil industry deregulation.
Viray said the oil companies would need to draw 85 million pesos from the fund for their transactions from Aug 1 to 13.
After Aug 13, the OPSF would be used to absorb oil price increases in excess of 59 centavos per liter.

Petron Corp still has the biggest claims from the oil fund at 1.04 billion pesos as of July followed by Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp., a unit of Royal Dutch Shell group . Caltex (Philippines) Inc, a joint venture between U.S.-based Chevron and Texaco Inc has claims amounting to 365.50 million pesos.

Energy Minister Francisco Viray said the energy department is still awaiting the response of the companies to its third request for a full or partial write-off of the claims. The department has written to the refiners thrice seeking for condonation of the claims.
Government is looking at appropriation of funds from Congress to pay off the oil firms if they refused a write-off.
